name: runheed
description: Production error tracking you can read in plain language. Ask what is breaking, read an error with its stack trace and the steps that led to it, see trends and project health, and mark an error resolved with a note of the fix.

interface.longDescription:
Runheed records the errors your Node.js and Python apps throw in production, groups repeats into one issue, and keeps each one with its stack trace, the breadcrumbs that led to it and the request it failed on. Here you can ask about them in plain language.

Things you can ask:
- What's breaking in production right now?
- Show me the top error with its stack trace and what happened just before it.
- Which errors started in the last 24 hours, and is the error rate going up?
- How healthy is the shop-api project?
- Mark the cart total error resolved with a note that it's fixed.

Resolving, ignoring and un-ignoring an error can all be undone. Runheed never changes your code or your servers; it only stores the errors your apps send to it.

Who it's for: developers who ship Node.js or Python backends and want to read and triage production errors in a conversation.

Limitations: requires a Runheed account with an app sending errors, set up at runheed.com.
capabilities: Search production errors by status and text
Read an error with its stack trace, breadcrumbs and request
See error trends over 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days
Resolve, ignore or un-ignore an error with a note
defaultPrompt: What's breaking in production right now?
Show me the top error and what led up to it
Which errors started in the last 24 hours?

positive.prompt: What's breaking in production right now?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the sample project's unresolved errors, most frequent first: TypeError "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'total')" (318 events), TimeoutError "Request to payments.example timed out after 10000ms" (41) and ValidationError "zip must be 5 digits" (7). Nothing is changed.

positive.prompt: What are the most recent errors in my apps?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the sample project's errors with the newest first, each with its type, message, event count and when it was last seen, including one already resolved ReferenceError in the account route. Nothing is changed.

positive.prompt: Show me the top error with its stack trace and what happened just before it.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the TypeError thrown in calculateTotals when an order is placed, with the breadcrumbs showing a coupon removed the only item in the cart just before. Nothing is changed.

positive.prompt: How healthy is the shop-api project, and are errors going up?
positive.expected_behavior: Gives the project's health score with its reasons and the error counts over the period asked. Nothing is changed.

positive.prompt: Mark the cart total TypeError resolved with the note: empty carts now return a 400 before totals are calculated.
positive.expected_behavior: Marks the TypeError resolved with that note and confirms it. It can be reopened by un-resolving it in Runheed; the sample data also resets every night.

negative.description: General knowledge has nothing to do with the user's errors. Runheed should not be called.
Writing new code from scratch is not an error lookup. The model should answer directly without calling Runheed.
negative.prompt: Write a JavaScript function that debounces another function.

negative.description: Runheed has no tool that deletes errors or projects. The model should say it can't delete them here, without changing anything.
negative.prompt: Delete every error in my Runheed account.

review.commerce_description: Runheed does not sell, offer or display anything for purchase inside ChatGPT. It only reads and updates the signed-in user's own error data. No prices or payment links appear in tool responses or in the sign-in flow when used from ChatGPT.

publication.release_notes: First release: 9 tools to read, triage and resolve the production errors in your Runheed account.
